about.title: Sounding out words with I and O
about.length_note: About 10 minutes fits the material: two new vowel sounds, six words, and a short review of the A words from the last class. You can pause after any step and come back. Nothing here is timed.

say.text: Hello {name}. Welcome to class 5. Last time we sounded out words with the letter A, like cat and map. Today we meet two more letters: I and O. Go at your own speed. You can stop and rest whenever you like.
First, a quick warm-up with A. The letter A makes the sound 'a', like at the start of 'apple'. Let's sound out c, a, t. Cuh... a... t. Cat.

show.text:
c – a – t = cat
m – a – p = map
h – a – t = hat

say.text: Well done. Which word has the A sound in the middle? Have a look, then choose.

ask.q: Which word has the A sound in the middle?
ask.why: Map is m-a-p. The middle letter is A, which says 'a'. Sit, dog and top have I or O in the middle.

say.text: Now a new letter: I. Here it makes a short sound, 'i', like at the start of 'itch' or in the middle of 'sit'. Say it with me: i, i, i. Your mouth is only open a little.
Let's join sounds to read 'sit'. s... i... t. Slide them together: sit. Now 'pin'. p... i... n. Pin. And 'big'. b... i... g. Big.

show.text:
s – i – t = sit
p – i – n = pin
b – i – g = big

say.text: Your turn. Sound out the word on the screen, one letter at a time, then join it up.

ask.q: Sound out p – i – n. What is the word?
ask.why: The sounds are p, i, n. Joined together they make 'pin'. The middle letter I says 'i'.

say.text: Next letter: O. It makes a short, round sound, 'o', like at the start of 'octopus' or in the middle of 'dog'. Your mouth opens wider and a little round. Say it: o, o, o. Some people say this sound a little differently depending on where they grew up. That is fine.
Let's read three O words. d... o... g. Dog. h... o... t. Hot. t... o... p. Top.

show.text:
d – o – g = dog
h – o – t = hot
t – o – p = top

say.text: Here is one to try. Look at the letters, say each sound, then join them.

ask.q: Sound out h – o – t. What is the word?
ask.why: The sounds are h, o, t. The middle letter O says 'o', so the word is 'hot'.

say.text: Now the clever part: telling A, I and O words apart. Look at these three words. Only the middle letter changes: hat, hit, hot. The middle letter tells you which sound to say.

show.text:
hat – A says 'a'
hit – I says 'i'
hot – O says 'o'

say.text: Try another set: tap, tip, top. Look at the middle letter each time. Which word has the O?

ask.q: Which of these words has the letter O in the middle?
ask.why: Top is t-o-p, with O in the middle. Tap has A and tip has I.

say.text: One more check. Which word has the I sound in the middle? Think about the sound as well as the letter.

ask.q: Which word says 'sit', with the I sound in the middle?
ask.why: Sit is s-i-t. The letter I says 'i'. Sat has A in the middle, and 'sot' and 'set' are not the word you wanted.

say.text: Lovely work, {name}. Today you learned that I says 'i' and O says 'o', and that the middle letter tells you which sound to say. You can read sit, pin, big, dog, hot and top. Next time we meet U and E. Rest well, and come back whenever you like.

show.text:
A – cat, map, hat
I – sit, pin, big
O – dog, hot, top
